situation.en: 262 armed incidents were reported in Ukraine and Russia in the past seven days, roughly as many as the week before. Most were armed clashs (68%), followed by armed assaults (21%). 89 of them were carried by two or more outlets. The most reported locations over the past month were Kyiv, Moscow and Odesa. UCDP lists 3 active armed conflicts here, the oldest dating from 1991. The most widely covered story this week: “Ukraine warns Trump-Putin diesel deal will bankroll Russia’s war” (Al Jazeera, 9 outlets).
situation.nb: 262 væpnede hendelser ble meldt i Ukraina og Russland de siste sju dagene, omtrent like mange som uken før. Flest gjaldt væpnet sammenstøt (68 prosent), deretter væpnet angrep (21 prosent). 89 av dem ble omtalt av to eller flere medier. De mest omtalte stedene den siste måneden var Kyiv, Moscow og Odesa. UCDP fører 3 aktive væpnede konflikter her, den eldste fra 1991. Mest omtalte sak denne uken: «Ukraine warns Trump-Putin diesel deal will bankroll Russia’s war» (Al Jazeera, 9 medier).

background.title: Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)
background.extract: On 24 February 2022, Russia invaded Ukraine, starting the largest and deadliest war in Europe since World War II, in a major escalation of the existing war between the two countries that began when Russia attacked Ukraine in 2014. The fighting has caused hundreds of thousands of military casualties and tens of thousands of Ukrainian civilian casualties. Russian troops occupy roughly 20% of Ukraine. From a population of 41 million, about 8 million Ukrainians have been internally displaced and 6–7 million have fled the country, creating Europe's largest refugee crisis since World War II.
